terra.problem: The comparison between warm ears and a cold cookie has no clear shared action or point, so the joke does not pass the joke logic test.
Job says no rod of punishment is upon them, not that it never shows up.
Saying they want a payoff before they will pray adds a condition the text does not state.
The claim that God gives so much is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
Job asks that the man himself be repaid; the explanation states that the punishment lands on him rather than his children as a fact.
Never tasting prosperity does not establish that the man never experienced any good things.
Saying Job means for the contrast to sting assigns him an unstated intention.
The man who never tasted prosperity is described as having nothing, which goes beyond the text.
Calling the first man someone who had it all goes beyond Job's description of him.
The text does not say the travelers have seen other towns and houses, or that Job sends his friends to question them.
The claim about what Job's friends keep insisting draws on other passages and needs a reference.
The explanation states as fact that the evil man's being spared is exactly why Job is troubled. The text does not make that precise connection.
The passage does not say the burial was not quick or that nobody stops the man on the way.
The passage says people follow behind him, but it does not establish that the goodbye was unhurried or that nobody was hurrying off.
